text:
After a week of use, here’s my honest review of the Asus Dual OC RTX 5060, which I got for €272 on sale from Amazon. It also came with a free Asus TUF M3 Gen II mouse, a nice extra to have as a backup.

🔧 I upgraded from an RX 6650 XT, and the difference is huge. The RTX 5060 delivers a much smoother experience, especially when it comes to 1% lows, which are rock solid now. With the 6650 XT, I was getting frequent drops. Cooling is also excellent: 30 °C idle with the fans off, and no more than 40-45 °C under load, even in demanding games.

📈 Game performance:

Valorant (low settings)

RX 6650 XT: ~240 FPS, not stable

RTX 5060: 500+ stable FPS


Fortnite (performance mode)

RX 6650 XT: 240–300 FPS with drops down to 110

RTX 5060: 400–600 FPS stable



In AAA titles, the performance gain is around 20–30% in favor of the RTX 5060. And that’s without even using DLSS. With DLSS enabled, the gap becomes even wider.

🖥️ All tests were done using a Ryzen 5 7600. Keep in mind, the RX 6650 XT had Smart Access Memory (SAM) enabled, yet the RTX 5060 still came out on top across the board.

🔚 Bottom line: I don’t regret the upgrade at all. Fantastic performance, great thermals, and rock-solid stability. A top-tier GPU for 1080p competitive gaming and beyond.

​ @VoornePuttenBenchmarks  " litteraly the worst choice for a handheld gpu, rtx 40 series does much, much better at lower wattages". Yes and no, 30 series was built on Samsung's 8nm process which is more like TSMCs 10nm-12nm process, 40 series was built on TSMCs much better 5nm process. Most (but not all) of the efficiency gains come from the node, not the "generation". TSMCs 5nm/4nm/3nm process nodes are expensive and full, churning out chips for Nvidia, AMD, Apple etc, both consumer and enterprise chips, non-stop AI and datacenter chips on years worth of back-order. 

If Nintendo chose the 40 series and TSMCs 5nm. Switch 2's would be more expensive and always out of stock due to low wafer allocation. They had a choice between Samsung's widely available, mature and high yield 8nm or Samsungs more expensive and less mature 5nm. They chose 8nm, They'll probably make a Switch 2 OLED on Samsungs 5nm a few years down the line when that node is cheaper and more mature. 

Also, it takes at least 3-4 years to develop a console, they started developing the switch 2 around 2021, when the RTX 3000 series was the most advanced, hardware had to be finalized early.

The fact that the switch 2 is able to play cyberpunk 2077 and consume 10W max, CPU + GPU + RAM + Display + Storage + Speakers + Antennas + Fan......10W Max, PS5/XSX idle on their home screens using like 40-50W. 

That's crazy optimization, especially at 8nm Samsung which they had to tweak a bit, obviously 5nm TSMC 40 series would have been better, but not possible due to budget, development time and scarcity constraints. 

The performance per watt is okay, it's just the battery is tiny (20wh battery), If it had the steam decks (40-50wh) battery, it would get 4-5 hours of cyberpunk 2077 minimum.

You can't complain about high Nvidia prices and low stock, then complain about a company that chooses a path which keeps prices low and stocks high.
